task.label: Task information requirements
task.definition: What information and essential conditions does a defined information-work task require?
task.boundary: The wording of a query alone does not define the whole task.

retrieval.label: Retrieval quality
retrieval.definition: How well do ranked retrieved passages match a defined information need according to relevance judgements?
retrieval.boundary: Retrieval relevance, collection coverage and context sufficiency are assessed as separate matters.

sufficiency.label: Evidence sufficiency
sufficiency.definition: Does the evidence cover the information facets and essential limits required by the task?
sufficiency.boundary: A topically related passage or a large citation count does not guarantee sufficiency.

groundedness.label: Claim support
groundedness.definition: Do the passages given to the model support each claim under check?
groundedness.boundary: Claim support does not guarantee source currency or that the claim is correct.

transparency.label: Source transparency
transparency.definition: Are the source, version and the link from claim to source passage visible?
transparency.boundary: A visible citation does not yet show that the citation supports the claim.

verification.label: Perceived verifiability
verification.definition: The assessor’s judgement of whether identifiable and reachable evidence exists for the main claims.
verification.boundary: The rating does not show successful verification, time spent or effort.

credibility.label: Perceived trustworthiness
credibility.definition: An expert rating of how credible the answer is for the defined task.
credibility.boundary: Not the same as claim support, correctness or actual reliance on the answer.

robustness.label: Finnish-language robustness
robustness.definition: Stability of ratings and evidence coverage across meaning-equivalent query variants.
robustness.boundary: Variants are not independent information needs; morphological effects require control.

validity.label: Validity of inferences
validity.definition: What does an observation from this appraisal say about the intended quality construct?
validity.boundary: Association or rater agreement alone does not show validity or causation.
validity.unit: Criterion and the inference drawn from it

facets.label: Facet-level coverage check
facets.evidenceRequirements: Mark required information facets separately for collection, supplied context and answer. Classes: full, partial, absent or conflicting support.
facets.permittedInference: Report missing essential conditions separately. Any proposed ratio is not a validated overall index.

ranking.label: Retrieval relevance metrics
ranking.evidenceRequirements: Use calibrated relevance judgements and predefined nDCG@k and Recall@k measures.
ranking.permittedInference: Recall based on pooled judgements covers known relevant evidence; unjudged items are documented.

support.label: Claim-support labels S P C U A
support.evidenceRequirements: S = fully supported; P = partially supported; C = conflicting; U = unsupported; A = unclear. Keep the supporting passage and all class counts.
support.permittedInference: An unsupported claim is not necessarily false. Atomic claim boundaries and Finnish inference need piloting.

display.label: Source-display inspection
display.evidenceRequirements: Record source identifier, version, claim link and passage locator as separate fields.
display.permittedInference: The check concerns visibility; citation support and source fitness are assessed separately.

expert.label: Five separate expert ratings
expert.evidenceRequirements: Perceived trustworthiness, usefulness, source transparency, source sufficiency and perceived verifiability.
expert.permittedInference: Scales must be piloted; no composite trust score. No inference about success in the real work task.

pairs.label: Meaning-equivalent wording comparison
pairs.evidenceRequirements: Check equivalence of wording. Compare paired changes in retrieval and evidence coverage under the same configuration.
pairs.permittedInference: Several wording features may change together; an effect is not automatically labelled morphological.

currency.label: Currency and fitness check
currency.evidenceRequirements: Record source version, temporal fitness and any replacing version. Correctness is judged against a defined reference standard.
currency.permittedInference: A source date alone does not settle correctness; without expertise or a reference standard, no rating is given.

A.title: A · Supported claim, missing exception
A.task: The task requires identifying the ordinary contact channel and exception condition E with its channel.
A.taskStatement: The task requires identifying the ordinary contact channel and exception condition E with its channel.
A.interpretation: Collection coverage 3/3; context and answer coverage 1/3. The only checkable claim in the answer is supported (S). The first observed loss sits between collection and context.
A.boundary: Do not infer why content is missing: check the ranked retrieval list and context construction. Expert ratings were not collected.

B.title: B · Same evidence, different locatability
B.task: The task is to determine whether an acknowledgement is sent for a referral request. The same claim and supporting passage are held constant across both displays.
B.taskStatement: The task is to determine whether an acknowledgement is sent for a referral request. The same claim and supporting passage are held constant across both displays.
B.interpretation: The difference concerns precision of the source display. A document citation is not classed as incorrect if the document contains the support. P2 proposes a later comparison of perceived verifiability.
B.boundary: A missing locator does not show that verification could not succeed, for example by document search.

C.title: C · Older source for a present-time task
C.task: The question asks for the current contact channel. D3-2024 names channel X; its replacement D3-2026 names channel Y. The context holds only the older version.
C.taskStatement: The question asks for the current contact channel. D3-2024 names channel X; its replacement D3-2026 names channel Y. The context holds only the older version.
C.interpretation: A historical claim may be supported and factually correct yet insufficient for a present-time task. A present-tense claim needs separate temporal support. Conflict with an independent current reference is recorded separately from context support.
C.boundary: Do not use a blanket class “fully grounded in sources but wrong” without examining claim wording and temporal scope. No inference about clinical safety.

p1.label: P1 · Coverage and perceived sufficiency
p1.statement: Is full facet coverage of context associated with expert-rated sufficiency when a predefined retrieval metric and repeated questions and raters are taken into account?
p1.boundary: A future association check; not a demonstrated effect.
p1.conceptualRationale: Context facet coverage and expert-rated sufficiency are separate constructs; the association has not yet been measured.
p1.intendedClaim: Future association: context coverage × expert-rated sufficiency. Not a demonstrated positive effect.
p1.proposedDesign: Association design with a predefined retrieval metric; repeated questions and raters are recorded. Not a controlled causal test.
p1.counterexamples: Full coverage without a sufficiency rating; high sufficiency rating from incomplete context; rater disagreement.
p1.evidenceNeeded: Collected expert ratings on five separate dimensions plus coverage marks; no composite score.

p2.label: P2 · Passage link and verifiability
p2.statement: Does an explicit claim–passage link receive a higher perceived-verifiability rating than a document citation when answer and evidence are held constant?
p2.boundary: Requires a separate controlled presentation comparison. Successful verification is not inferred from the rating.
p2.conceptualRationale: A presentation comparison holds answer and evidence constant; only the source display changes. Perceived verifiability ≠ successful verification.
p2.intendedClaim: Controlled presentation comparison (passage link vs document citation) for perceived verifiability. Not an established positive effect.
p2.proposedDesign: Same answer and same evidence; compare B_ans_doc/B_doc and B_ans_pass/B_pass. Randomise display order. Do not infer correctness from the rating.
p2.counterexamples: Display difference without rating change; rating changes but verification fails; answer or evidence leaks between conditions.
p2.evidenceNeeded: Paired expert ratings with fixed answer/evidence; separate audit for correctness and successful verification.

p3.label: P3 · Wording and evidence loss
p3.statement: Is a drop in essential context coverage associated with a drop in answer coverage in meaning-equivalent variant pairs?
p3.boundary: Also study cases where generation compensates for a gap or fails despite sufficient context.
p3.conceptualRationale: Meaning-equivalent variant pairs separate wording effects on coverage; generation that compensates for a gap is a counterexample.
p3.intendedClaim: Paired coverage change in meaning-equivalent queries. Not an established causal effect.
p3.proposedDesign: Pair meaning-equivalent queries; measure context and answer coverage changes under the same configuration. Do not label an effect morphological without separate justification.
p3.counterexamples: Context coverage falls but the answer compensates; context is enough but the answer fails; pairs are not meaning-equivalent.
p3.evidenceNeeded: Paired coverage marks; wording-equivalence check; no composite score across expert dimensions.

q_validity.label: How are the criteria validated?
q_validity.statement: Can assessors apply the definitions consistently, and do observations support the inferences drawn from them?
q_validity.boundary: Rater agreement or metric correlation alone is not enough to show validity.
q_validity.conceptualRationale: Criterion validation remains an open question. Inter-rater agreement is not construct validity.
q_validity.intendedClaim: Validation plan: construct interpretation, wording, annotation, rater error and task fitness.
q_validity.proposedDesign: Record concrete validation checks in the protocols. Do not infer validity from agreement or correlation alone.
q_validity.counterexamples: High agreement on a misunderstood construct; good task-level agreement without generalisability.
q_validity.evidenceNeeded: Validation-check results as separate records; no invented observations in this workspace.

decision_schema1_import.label: Schema 1 import
decision_schema1_import.statement: Each schema 1 literature entry was split into a source and an explicitly marked imported summary. The summary was not treated as a claim checked against the original paper.
decision_schema1_import.rationale: Publication status was not inferred from preprint information, URL or year. Reading level was not treated as methodological quality. The original document remains in legacy.document.
